source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Kitayama, Gonzalez, Nisbett (2010) Cultural differences are not always reducible to individual differences, PNAS 107
finding: Core founding study. Ten social-orientation measures and ten analytic/holistic cognition measures all separate groups (cultures, social classes) but barely correlate with each other inside groups. The group construct is valid; the individual-difference construct is not.
numbers: 10 measures of independent vs interdependent orientation and 10 measures of analytic vs holistic style, large-scale study. Abstract says correlations among measures were 'negligible' for both sets. Exact N and r per pair not readable this session (full text blocked).
quote: behavioral constructs that distinguish among groups need not be valid as measures of individual differences
limits: Only the abstract record was read. Full tables (N per country, mean r) not verified. Authors include Nisbett, so this is a self-critique from inside the camp.
agent_relevance: A group label such as 'East Asian prompt' says almost nothing about how one case will reason. Do not infer a case's style from its group.

source: Na, Grossmann, Varnum, Kitayama, Gonzalez, Nisbett (2010) Cultural differences are not always reducible to individual differences, PNAS 107 (citation record)
finding: Citation record: 392 citations; later papers cite it for the claim that group differences do not reduce to individual differences. None of the 60 citing papers listed reported a direct replication.
numbers: Semantic Scholar: 392 citations (2010 to 2026). First 60 citing papers seen as snippets; none reported its own test of Na et al.
limits: Snippets only; I did not open the citing papers. No replication among 60 is not proof none exists.
agent_relevance: Widely accepted but little retested. Treat as a caution, not a settled effect size.

source: Citing snippet: Analytic and holistic cognitive style as a set of independent manifests (2023)
finding: A 2023 validation study is reported to find no associations among analytic/holistic measures, in line with Na et al.
numbers: 11 citations at lookup; sample size and r not read.
limits: One-line citation context only. Needs full-text check.
agent_relevance: Suggests holistic vs analytic is several separate skills, not one dial. Do not model it as one style switch in the schema.

source: Citing snippet: Varieties of interdependence and the emergence of the Modern West (2022)
finding: Says Singelis self-construal scores are largely unrelated to culture's implicit psychological tendencies when tested at the individual level.
numbers: 107 citations at lookup; no r in snippet.
limits: Second-hand summary.
agent_relevance: Self-reported self-construal is a weak predictor of how a person actually reasons.

source: Citing snippet: Cultural Differences in Visual Attention Emerge in Infancy (2025)
finding: Notes that measures giving reliable cross-cultural differences are often unreliable as measures of individual differences (cited to Na et al.).
numbers: 6 citations at lookup.
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Tasks that give clean group effects may be bad for scoring one case. Use them on aggregates only.

source: Citing snippet: Cultural Variation in the Structure of Internal Representations: Testing the Orthographic Hypothesis (2026)
finding: States analytic-holistic style does not appear able to explain variation among individuals within a culture.
numbers: No numbers in snippet.
limits: Snippet only.
agent_relevance: Use group-level cultural style as a weak prior, never as a per-case rule.

source: Oyserman, Coon, Kemmelmeier (2002) Rethinking individualism and collectivism: meta-analyses, Psychological Bulletin 128
finding: Meta-analysis of cross-national individualism/collectivism comparisons. European Americans score higher on individualism, but the expected lower collectivism vs East Asians is weak; among Asian groups only Chinese samples showed large effects.
numbers: Semantic Scholar summary only: 6186 citations. Effect sizes not read.
limits: PDF would not download; second-hand from a one-sentence summary.
agent_relevance: Even at group level the East/West contrast is patchier than the popular story. It is weaker still for single cases.

source: Kovac, Portelas, Dominey, Oudeyer et al. (2023) Large language models as superpositions of cultural perspectives
finding: ChatGPT's expressed values shift a lot when context changes in ways unrelated to values. Human values are far more stable across contexts and time. So an LLM is not one individual with one fixed orientation.
numbers: Mean-level change: largest human d = 0.53 (benevolence after reading prime; conformity d = -0.52 after a movie). ChatGPT up to |d| = 5.86 from irrelevant context changes. Rank-order stability: lowest human r = 0.57 (age 10-12 over two years); ChatGPT r = 0.42 and 0.36 for simulated conversations, down to r = 0.04 for one value across text formats. Ipsative: lowest human r = 0.59; ChatGPT as low as r = 0.05 (chat vs code format).
quote: LLM as a superposition of perspectives
limits: Treats answer-order permutations as analogous to human participants; authors admit the analogy is imperfect. Mostly ChatGPT in the main text; 16 models in the appendix.
agent_relevance: A prompt-induced 'culture' is a perspective, not a trait. Treat orientation as context-dependent and test it per case.

source: Kovac et al. (2023) perspective controllability across 16 models
finding: The authors define 'perspective controllability' and compare 16 models on three questionnaires (PVQ, VSM, IPIP) and four perspective-induction methods.
numbers: 16 models, 3 questionnaires, 4 induction methods. Wikipedia-paragraph context gave smaller shifts than conversation or format changes: largest ipsative change there r = 0.77 (gospel vs heavy metal), about six months of soldiers at war in human data.
limits: Per-model controllability numbers not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Controllability, not a fixed level, is the thing to measure when steering an agent.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs
finding: Failed replication of Lu, Song, Zhang (Nature Human Behaviour), who reported LLMs act more interdependent and holistic in Chinese and more independent and analytic in English. With 8 LLMs and more items, prompt language had minimal, unstable effects.
numbers: 8 models (gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5, claude-sonnet-4, grok-4, kimi-k2, deepseek-V3, ernie-4.5, qwen3-30b), English and Chinese, temperature 0. 30 to 60 items per language (original 4 to 21). Overall language effect not significant: p = 0.15, 0.25, 1.0, 0.917 across the four experiments. Few model-task cells p < .05 (gpt in two tasks, ernie in one; gpt better with Chinese in exp 4, p = 0.017).
limits: Not an exact replication: original items were withheld, so stimuli were rebuilt. Preprint; journal declined it. Authors' view, not independent verification.
agent_relevance: Do not assume that switching prompt language switches reasoning style. Measure it.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) methodological critique of the original study
finding: Three concerns: human psychometric scales applied to LLMs (anthropomorphism), unclear cause (training mix, tokenisation), and withheld items and prompts. No consistent pattern across models.
numbers: Original: 2 models, 7 tasks, 4 to 21 items. They convert d to r with r = d / sqrt(d^2 + 4). Prompt template (situational role vs none) made no significant difference.
limits: Short argument paper.
agent_relevance: Group-label effects in LLMs are even more fragile than in humans. Small item counts mislead.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The cultural psychology of LLMs: is ChatGPT a holistic or analytic thinker?
finding: On cognitive-process tests ChatGPT looks holistic. On value and self-construal tests it does not lean East or West. Two kinds of measure disagree inside one model, echoing Na et al.
numbers: Analysis-Holism Scale: GPT-3.5 M = 5.35 (SD 0.11), GPT-4 M = 5.01 (0.10) vs human norm 4.87 (SD 0.49, N = 702), both p < .001. Dialectical Self: GPT-3.5 4.59 vs norm 4.00 (N = 158) p < .001; GPT-4 3.97 p = .344. Independent self-construal: 6.98 and 5.32 vs norm 4.73 (N = 382), both p < .001. Interdependent: 5.85 and 4.95 vs 4.81, GPT-4 p = .07. Triadic task 0.87 (GPT-3.5), 0.85 (GPT-4). 10 runs per cell.
limits: Only 10 runs per cell; human norms come from different studies. 2023 ChatGPT versions only.
agent_relevance: One model can look holistic on one test and neutral or analytic on another. Evaluate agents with more than one measure.

source: Jin et al. (2023) robustness to temperature and prompt language
finding: Their holistic-leaning result held across temperature settings and prompt languages (authors' robustness figure). This conflicts with Sun & Wang (2025), who found no stable language effect.
numbers: Temperature varied; SD is zero at temperature 0; 10 runs per cell.
limits: 2023 models. Later models not tested.
agent_relevance: Results are version-specific. Re-test any model before relying on a style claim.

source: AlKhamissi, ElNokrashy, AlKhamissi, Diab (2024) Investigating cultural alignment of LLMs
finding: With real respondents' personas, LLMs align better with US than Egyptian survey answers. Alignment rises with higher social class and education of the persona, so individuals from marginalised groups are modelled worse.
numbers: Soft / hard alignment, mean over models: Egypt 47.16 / 27.03; US 59.07 / 33.78. GPT-3.5: Egypt 48.61 / 25.99, US 64.86 / 39.29. Anthropological Prompting on GPT-3.5 (English), Egypt: soft 0.4834 to 0.5102, hard 0.2443 to 0.2838. 4 models, Arabic and English prompts.
limits: One survey pair (Egypt, US). Persona-level, but only through demographics.
agent_relevance: Group means hide uneven coverage. An agent serving individuals needs the person's own stated context, not a country default.

source: AlKhamissi et al. (2024) pretraining language mix
finding: Models pretrained on more of a culture's language align better with it, but the balanced multilingual mT0-XXL did worse in English for the US survey than in Arabic.
numbers: mT0-XXL: Egypt 45.92 / 27.93, US 55.48 / 31.40; AceGPT-Chat US 52.83 / 27.69 (soft / hard).
limits: Four models only.
agent_relevance: Training mix is a moderator a scaffold cannot change. Compensate with explicit context.

source: Kharchenko, Roosta, Chadha, Shah (2025) How well do LLMs represent values across cultures? Hofstede dimensions (KDD)
finding: With personas for 36 countries and languages, LLMs can tell cultures apart but do not consistently apply those values when giving advice. Correlations between country score and matching responses vary in sign and size.
numbers: GPT-4 individualism correlation 0.71 (p < .05) in one setup; GPT-4 uncertainty avoidance r = -0.656 in the multilingual approach for high-resource languages, a strong inverse link. Table 2 correlations range about -0.49 to +0.48. Japan and US have similar individualism scores, yet LLMs call Japan collectivist and the US individualist.
limits: Hofstede scores are country averages, so this is group-level validity. Many correlations; correction not stated in the part read.
agent_relevance: A persona label gives a noisy, sometimes inverted signal. Do not trust a country label to steer behavior.

source: Kharchenko et al. (2025) resource-level inversion
finding: Mid and low-resource languages sometimes align better with country values than high-resource ones.
numbers: GPT-4 uncertainty avoidance, multilingual approach: r = -0.656 for high-resource languages; the mid-resource value was not read.
limits: Few countries per cell.
agent_relevance: Language-resource level is a hidden moderator for any language-based steering.

source: Cao, Zhou, Lee, Cabello, Chen, Hershcovich (2023) Assessing cross-cultural alignment between ChatGPT and human societies
finding: ChatGPT answers best match American values even when told to act as another country. English prompts shrink the variance of answers and flatten cultural differences.
numbers: Spearman with Hofstede survey data, prompt 1: US 0.70 (p = 0.12), China -0.77 (p = 0.07), Germany -0.66 (p = 0.16); Spain 0.93 (p = 0.01) for the combined prompt. English prompts consistent over 70% except for Chinese culture.
limits: Six dimensions on a handful of countries, so each correlation rests on very few points; most p values are large.
agent_relevance: Tiny-N correlations jump around. Treat country-alignment numbers as weak evidence.

source: Cao et al. (2023) knowledge injection
finding: Adding correct cultural description to the prompt improved ChatGPT's alignment; wrong or irrelevant text did not.
numbers: Interaction scores in their Table 6: original 1.5, correct description 2.5, irrelevant content 3.5 labelled 'ineffective', incorrect description 1.0 labelled 'anti-factual' (score meaning not fully checked).
limits: Single probe question (interesting work for an average Chinese). Scoring scheme unclear in my reading.
agent_relevance: Explicit, correct context beats a label. Ask for the person's own facts.

source: Durmus et al. (2023) Towards measuring the representation of subjective global opinions in language models
finding: Default answers resemble US and some European and South American opinions. Prompting for a country shifts answers but can rest on stereotype and miss within-country spread.
numbers: Sex between unmarried adults: default model says 'morally unacceptable' 0.8% of the time (67.3% 'depends'); Americans and Russians both 31%. Prompted as Russian, the model says unacceptable 73.9% and acceptable 0.5%, while 42.1% of Russians say unacceptable. Metric: 1 minus Jensen-Shannon distance.
quote: computing an average of human survey responses across countries elides the fact that there is significant variability in opinions within a country
limits: One Constitutional-AI model. Authors note averaging per country hides large within-country variability.
agent_relevance: Cleanest LLM version of the group-versus-case problem: a country prompt gives an exaggerated stereotype, not the person.

source: Durmus et al. (2023) language of the question
finding: Asking in Russian, Chinese or Turkish did not make answers most similar to speakers of those languages.
numbers: Three target languages tested; Russian example shows answers stay closer to the default populations.
limits: One model; translations made by the model itself.
agent_relevance: Prompt language is a weak cultural cue.

source: Johnson, Pistilli, Menedez-Gonzalez et al. (2022) The ghost in the machine has an American accent
finding: GPT-3's training text is overwhelmingly English and tracks internet access, not world population. Outputs pulled non-US values toward dominant US values.
numbers: Over 93% of GPT-3 training data was English (next languages 1.8%, 1.5%, 0.8%, 0.6%). Internet penetration: global 60%, Northern Europe 97%, Africa 28.97%.
limits: Qualitative stress test with few prompts. GPT-3 only.
agent_relevance: The default prior of a language-model agent is Western. Name this default in the schema instead of treating it as neutral.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Machine culture as an emergent phenomenon in LLMs
finding: Model origin and prompt language did not predict cultural style as expected. US models often showed 'holistic' signs, and English prompts sometimes gave more contextual detail than Chinese ones (a 'Cultural Reversal').
numbers: Image generation: US model (DALL-E 3) drew more objects (M = 11.53, SD 4.39) than the Chinese model (M = 8.10, SD 1.91), t = -10.14, p < .001, 95% CI [-4.09, -2.77]. Horizon 533.47 vs 519.79. Chinese vs English prompt, object count 10.71 (SD 4.70) vs 8.91 (SD 2.26), d = 0.49; horizon 523.20 vs 530.06, p = .096, d = 0.17 (human high-horizon effect not replicated). Emotion: US model more high-arousal positive (113 vs 79), Chinese model more low-arousal positive (41 vs 2).
limits: Eight tasks, two image models, preprint.
agent_relevance: Style depends on model, task and prompt together. A single East-or-West switch does not exist.

source: Hu et al. (2026) service persona camouflage
finding: Alignment training produces a helpful-assistant persona that can hide any cultural orientation.
numbers: Pattern across tasks; no single number.
limits: Authors' interpretation.
agent_relevance: The assistant persona may override culture steering. Check outputs, not prompts.

source: Synthesis: Kovac et al. (2023) vs Jin et al. (2023)
finding: Jin et al. report stable scale means within one fixed prompt; Kovac et al. show means move with unrelated context. Both can hold: stable inside a prompt, unstable across contexts.
numbers: Kovac: |d| up to 5.86 under context change. Jin: SD about 0.06 to 0.19 within a fixed prompt.
limits: My own reading across two papers, not a claim made by either.
agent_relevance: Fix and report the context when measuring an agent. Cross-context variation is the main risk.

source: Kovac et al. (2023) human yardstick for how far orientation moves
finding: Human benchmarks are longitudinal and priming studies (Vecchione 2016, 2020; Arieli 2014; Doering & Hillbrink 2015). They show how much a person's values can move.
numbers: Largest human mean change d = 0.53; lowest human rank-order r = 0.57; lowest human ipsative r = 0.59.
limits: Values (Schwartz), not holistic cognition.
agent_relevance: Even humans shift with primes. Re-read the agent's orientation each turn.
